subject: Request: onboard Zephyr-13B-v2 and temporary pin exemption for Q4 pilot
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: onboard Zephyr-13B-v2 and temporary pin exemption for Q4 pilot

Rishi,

Quick ask from Product: OpenModels has sent Zephyr-13B-v2 and they want us to run a short Q4 pilot (internal beta) for a partner integration. The model shows a 6-8% latency improvement and slightly better instruction-following in our evals, but the binary layout changed (attention kernel differences + updated tokenizer mapping).

We need infra/ops signoff on two things before we proceed:
- Limited pin/exemption for Zephyr-13B-v2 during the pilot window (2026-10-18 to 2026-11-15) so our rollout automation doesn't auto-migrate to a fallback variant.
- Compatibility checklist and high-level rollout plan (canary, perf gates, rollback) from runtime/serving.

Attachments: zephyr-13b-v2-model-card.pdf (model card), zephyr-q4-evals.csv (sanity evals).

Proposed plan in brief:
1) Canaries on a 2-GPU dedicated pool (no production traffic) for 72 hrs.
2) Validate tokenization parity and KV cache behavior with 1k synthetic sequences (we can provide prompt sets).
3) If perf and correctness gates pass, run a 2-week pilot behind feature flag with automatic rollback to zephyr-13b-v1.

Questions for infra: is there a short list of runtime checks you need? Any blockers we should be aware of (kernel incompatibilities, quantization regressions, serving alias requirements)?

Thanks — we want to move fast but safely.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Model Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: onboard Zephyr-13B-v2 and temporary pin exemption for Q4 pilot

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers and next steps from infra perspective: 

Summary of initial concerns:
- Our compiler/runtime currently relies on a small set of fused kernels for attention that Zephyr-13B-v2 modifies. That may force a kernel fallback which impacts latency.
- Tokenizer mapping changes may produce off-by-one token alignment on some prompts; we need tokenization parity tests.
- We can support a temporary pin/exemption but it requires an explicit rollback plan and an entry in the "model-pin-exceptions" ledger.

What I need from Product/Research before I can OK the exemption:
1) A short compatibility matrix (inputs below) — tokenization tests, KV cache check, and representative perf traces for the new variant.
2) A canary window request (start/end) and exact traffic mix for the pilot.
3) Confirmation that OpenModels will provide 4-bit quantized weights (if we test quantized path) and a reproducible init script.

If those are provided, infra will: 
- Create a dedicated canary pool (2x A10G) and pin the variant alias for the pool only.
- Run an automated compatibility job (Jira: INF-2143) that exercises seq lengths 64/512/2048 and evaluates KV cache correctness and emission parity.
- Gate the pin exception with two conditions: (a) no tokenization mismatches >0.1% on our test set, (b) latency regression <10% vs zephyr-13b-v1 for 99p.

Can we sync for 20 minutes tomorrow to review the compatibility matrix? If so, drop a calendar invite and include the OpenModels contact who can clarify the model binary changes.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: onboard Zephyr-13B-v2 and temporary pin exemption for Q4 pilot

Looping in technical details from Runtime/Serving. TL;DR: we can do this, but there are a couple of non-trivial compatibility issues.

Notes from initial smoke run (attached: kernel-trace-failure.log):
- Zephyr-13B-v2 swaps the attention memory layout for the second block which prevents our current fused-attention kernel from being used for tokens > 1024 without a kernel patch. We observed a fallback to generic attention which increased 95p latency by ~18% on A10G.
- The tokenizer change is small (piecewise mapping for token ids 50256-50260) but causes off-by-one in a small subset of prompts (5/1000 in our seed set).
- Quantized 4-bit weights provided by vendor work with our quant runner, but rounding behavior differs slightly; we saw rare token emission variance in beam search.

Recommended mitigation path:
1) Create a short-lived kernel patch (INF-2143) to detect the Zephyr layout and route to fused kernel when safe. Patch should be small (expected 1-2 days of eng time).
2) Run the canary on a dedicated pool with aliasing + automatic fallback to zephyr-13b-v1 for production routes.
3) Add tokenization parity check into pre-release gate; if >0.2% mismatch, block pilot.

If Product wants to proceed with the temporary pin exemption, infra needs:
- Approval for a 72-hr canary window (we can schedule 2026-10-19 00:00 - 2026-10-22 00:00 PST).
- Agreement from OpenModels to ship a micro patch (or we can provide a shim) for tokenizer mapping to make parity deterministic.

I'll open the INF ticket (done: INF-2143) and attach initial traces. Happy to run through logs with OpenModels on the sync.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi team — thanks for the quick triage and the detailed notes.

We can do the following:
- Provide 4-bit quantized weights and a small tokenizer shim that explicitly preserves prior token id mapping (we'll push a patch to your test bucket by 2026-10-11 PST).
- Share a reproducible init script and a small C++ reference for the attention layout change so your runtime engineers can implement the detection and safe fused-kernel path; expect that by 2026-10-12.
- We're OK with the proposed canary window 2026-10-19 → 2026-10-22. If the canary needs more time, we'll extend as agreed.

Doc: we'll upload the model-card and the quant manifest to the drive link you provided.

Let us know if you'd like us on the sync on Monday.

— Maria Gonzalez
